The fixture turns the holder 1.25 turns while arm 1 holds the crucible still: the thread's engagement is tiny, "you just barely have to get it on" (T8 2:26). It stops at the torque limit, 0.40 N m (assumed): overtightening cracks the holder's thread (T9 33:45).

Thread finding, as a person does it: a light push up, the nut turned backwards until it drops onto the thread's start, then forward. Torque that rises in the first turn would mean a crossed thread: back off.

Thread finding, as a person does it: a light push up, the nut turned backwards until it drops onto the thread's start, then forward. Torque that rises in the first turn would mean a crossed thread: back off.
The key's motor runs the nut up 6.5 turns, 2.0 mm a turn (13 mm), the arm rising with it. Arm 1 holds the crucible still and reads the thread's drag.
Before the nut is tight, arm 1 turns the crucible 90 deg clockwise so its thermocouple hole comes to the port at the back right; the key holds the nut, so the joint draws up 0.5 mm (SOP 3).
Before the nut is tight, arm 1 turns the crucible 90 deg clockwise so its thermocouple hole comes to the port at the back right; the key holds the nut, so the joint draws up 0.5 mm (SOP 3).
Snug: the key turns the nut the last 54 deg to the torque limit, 0.30 N m (assumed: our bench-test start value), read by arm 1's FT 300-S through the crucible. Then it stops.

The key lets go: it drops 16 mm so the pins and the cup clear the nut, and goes out through the door. Arm 1 opens its jaws and lifts the gripper off; the crucible stays on its thread.
